intro.heading: Understanding Scheme Documents — SID, SAI & KIM
intro.subtitle: A Complete Guide to Mutual Fund Offer Documents | Mandatory Reading Before Every Investment
intro.summaryLine: Innovate Securities Pvt. Ltd. | ARN-42505 | www.innovatesec.com | Last Updated: August 2026
intro.notice: SEBI regulations mandate that every Mutual Fund scheme must have three offer documents — SID, SAI, and KIM. These contain risks, costs, objectives, and terms. Innovate Securities strongly encourages every investor to read these documents before investing. We will provide any of these documents on request within 24 hours — free of charge.

blocks.heading: The Three Mandatory Mutual Fund Documents

items.title: SID — Scheme Information Document
items.body: The most detailed document for a specific scheme — objectives, risks, costs, and fund manager details. Most Important.

items.title: SAI — Statement of Additional Information
items.body: General information about the AMC and Mutual Fund — legal, tax, and KYC information. AMC-level.

items.title: KIM — Key Information Memorandum
items.body: Concise 1–2 page summary of critical facts, attached to the application form. Quick reference.

blocks.heading: 1. Scheme Information Document (SID) — In Detail
blocks.intro: The SID is the primary legal document for a Mutual Fund scheme. Every SID contains:
bullets: Investment Objective — growth, income, capital preservation, or a combination
Asset Allocation Pattern — equity, debt, derivatives, REITs, etc.
Risk Factors & SEBI Riskometer — market, credit, interest rate, liquidity risks
Total Expense Ratio (TER) — Direct Plan and Regular Plan
Exit Load Structure — charges on early redemption
Benchmark Index — e.g. Nifty 50, BSE Sensex, Nifty 500
Fund Manager Details — name, qualifications, experience
Historical NAV Performance — 1 / 3 / 5 year and since inception
Dividend / IDCW History
Minimum Investment Amounts — lumpsum, SIP, additional purchase
Redemption & Settlement — T+1 / T+2, cut-off times
Fundamental Attributes — core characteristics requiring investor consent to change

blocks.heading: 2. Statement of Additional Information (SAI) — In Detail
blocks.intro: The SAI contains general information about the AMC and all its schemes:
bullets: AMC & Trustee Company Details — CIN, address, board, key personnel
Sponsor Information
Rights of Unit Holders
Tax Treatment of MF Investments — STCG and LTCG
KYC Requirements — FATCA/CRS, NRI norms
Penalties & Pending Litigation against the AMC
Investor Grievance Mechanism and SEBI SCORES details
AML / KYC Policy of the AMC
Associate Transactions — related-party disclosures

blocks.heading: 3. Key Information Memorandum (KIM) — In Detail
blocks.intro: The KIM is a summarised document attached to every Mutual Fund application form:
bullets: Investment Objective (summary)
Asset Allocation Table
SEBI Riskometer — 6-level risk label
Current NAV — Direct and Regular Plans
Benchmark Index and Fund Manager Name
Exit Load and Minimum Investment Amounts
Plans Available — Direct Plan and Regular Plan
IDCW option details
Standard MF disclaimer

blocks.heading: Quick Comparison — SID vs SAI vs KIM

items.title: Low
items.body: Overnight / Liquid funds — very short duration, highly liquid, minimal risk

items.title: Low to Moderate
items.body: Ultra Short Duration, Money Market, Short Duration — low interest rate risk

items.title: Moderate
items.body: Balanced / Conservative Hybrid, Medium Duration — balanced risk

items.title: Moderately High
items.body: Large Cap, Flexi Cap, Aggressive Hybrid — equity with moderate-high risk

items.title: High
items.body: Mid Cap, Multi Cap, ELSS, Thematic — significant market risk

items.title: Very High
items.body: Small Cap, Sector/Thematic, International — highest market risk

blocks.body: The Riskometer is updated monthly by AMCs based on portfolio composition. Always check the current Riskometer before investing. Regulatory basis: SEBI Circular SEBI/HO/IMD/DF2/CIR/P/2020/253 dated December 31, 2020.

items.title: Know Your Risks
items.body: The Riskometer and risk factors section tell you exactly what risks you are taking. Never invest without understanding them.

items.title: Know Your Costs
items.body: TER, exit load, and transaction charges are clearly disclosed. Higher costs reduce your net returns significantly over time.

items.title: Check Suitability
items.body: The investment objective tells you if the scheme matches your financial goal — wealth creation, income, or capital preservation.

items.title: Understand Lock-in
items.body: ELSS has 3-year lock-in. Close-ended funds have fixed maturity. Know before you invest — liquidity matters.

items.title: Verify Fund Manager
items.body: Fund manager changes significantly impact performance. Check who manages the fund and their track record in the SID.

items.title: Compare Options
items.body: Reading KIMs of similar schemes helps you compare TER, exit load, and performance across options before deciding.

blocks.heading: Innovate Securities’ Commitment
